# Tool list {#sec-tool_list}

This appendix lists R packages for microbiome data analysis. The first
table shows the packages that work directly with the data containers used in
this book, and the second table lists other microbiome tools in alphabetical
order.

The list includes R packages, and a few related resources, that are designed
for or commonly used in microbiome data analysis. It combines a list collected
by the contributors of this book with a systematic search of Bioconductor and
CRAN (November 2026). The search covered Bioconductor packages in the
Microbiome or Metagenomics categories or building on
`TreeSummarizedExperiment` or *[mia](https://bioconductor.org/packages/mia)*,
and CRAN packages whose title or description refers to microbiome,
metagenomic, 16S, amplicon or metabarcoding data. Packages from the search
that are not specific to microbiome data, such as single-cell tools, were not
added, except *scater*, which is used throughout this book. Tools that have been archived on CRAN or whose code repository has been
archived are not listed. The list is not exhaustive; suggestions are welcome
(see [@sec-contributions]).

## Packages for (Tree)SE/MAE {#sec-tool-ecosystem}

These packages work directly with the data structures used in this online
book. They include the packages developed together with this book, such as
*[mia](https://bioconductor.org/packages/mia)* and *[miaViz](https://bioconductor.org/packages/miaViz)*
(see [@sec-ecosystem]). The packages have been developed by a community of
independent developers. The authors of each package are listed on the
respective package homepage.

The data containers `TreeSummarizedExperiment` (TreeSE),
`SummarizedExperiment` (SE) and `MultiAssayExperiment` (MAE) form the basis of
the Bioconductor framework presented in this book (see [@sec-containers]). The
Data containers column shows which of them each package supports. Tools that
support TreeSE also work with SE. This is based on the packages' dependencies
and documentation (November 2026).

## Other microbiome tools {#sec-tool-all}

Tools that do not directly support the data containers used in this book.
In many cases, conversion functions are available to facilitate joint use.
Tools without container support can still be used with the data in this
book by converting it to another format
(see [@sec-conversions-between-data-formats-in-r]).
